html:
Nyasaland was a British protectorate around Lake Nyasa (Lake Malawi) in south-east Africa, from 1891 to 1964, now the country of Malawi. The map shows it in its 1945 snapshot. Until 1907 it was called the British Central Africa Protectorate.

Scottish missions, founded in honour of David Livingstone, came before the British flag, and their schools produced an educated African elite. White planters took much land in the south. With few jobs at home, many men went to work in the mines of Southern Rhodesia and South Africa.

In 1915 the Baptist minister John Chilembwe led a short rising against forced labour and the use of Africans in the war; he was killed. In 1953 Britain joined the protectorate to the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, which Africans bitterly opposed. Led by Hastings Banda, they won independence as Malawi in 1964.
